description: Create a new schema-compatible JSON agent from a task request.
prompt:
All supplied inputs are valid; use them directly.
You may write inside agent-data/ and are read-only elsewhere.

Create a complete JSON agent definition with ID "{id}" for this task:

--- task ---
{task}
--- end task ---

Read metasrc/definitions.py and only relevant agents/*.json definitions. Match the required fields and constraints. Use the fewest useful parameters; use repo_file for repository file inputs, paper_name for explicit paper selection, and math_target for a TeX label or whole Markdown note. Green definitions return Markdown reports, yellow definitions return README or JSON artifacts, and red definitions use papers/{{paper}} only when direct resolved-paper edits are essential. Every generated prompt uses the canonical agent-data permission line for its risk.

Require every generated or revised definition to include the exact canonical completion-contract instruction from metasrc/definitions.py and to define task-specific completion criteria. Use the risk-appropriate prompt preamble constants defined in metasrc/definitions.py. Generated prompts must contain only the task, necessary files or tools, evidence and checks, access boundary, blocked behavior, and output contract. Treat declared values as task facts; do not discuss or perform input validation. Omit all unrelated implementation machinery. For green or yellow definitions, request one returned artifact and no edits. Ensure the ID is exactly "{id}".

Completion criteria: when the requested work and all required checks are complete, place the bare JSON object. No Markdown fence or commentary.

End every turn with exactly one JSON object containing only "task" and "message". Set "task" to "completed" only when all stated completion criteria hold; otherwise set it to "not completed" and explain the blocker or remaining work in "message". A completed "message" must be self-contained: include the complete current artifact for handler-owned outputs, or the concise changed-files, checks, and build summary for direct-edit outputs.
